findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House concurrence in Senate committee substitute), roll call 801, passed 62-47
findings.note: Voted no on House concurrence in the Senate version of HB 958. Per the legislature's bill digest (https://webservices.ncleg.gov/BillDigests/2025/H958), the Senate version keeps the in-person photo ID rule (GS 163-166.16) and treats certain expired Class C drivers licenses as valid for it through 2027, extends the time to supply ID after a provisional ballot, requires an affirmative US-citizenship statement on voter registration, requires a full social security number to register, limits who may hand-deliver an absentee ballot to a near relative or legal guardian with an affidavit, and limits overseas-voter ID to specific documents with no affidavit option. The Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17 (https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/H958). This page shows only her vote, not her reasons.
subjects: absentee ballot delivery and ID for overseas voters
full social security number to register

findings.motion: HB 834 State Board of Elections Administrative Changes, M11 Concur (House concurrence in Senate committee substitute), roll call 800, passed 74-35
findings.note: Voted no on House concurrence in the Senate version of HB 834 (became SL 2026-60). Per the bill digest (https://webservices.ncleg.gov/BillDigests/2025/H834), it extends the deadline to fix a registration form, to supply ID when ID numbers do not match, and to supply ID after a provisional ballot, from the third to the fifth business day after an election, and treats certain expired Class C drivers licenses as valid for the in-person photo ID rule through 2027. Her vote is on file; her reasons are not on this page.

findings.motion: Co-sponsor of HB 691 Voter Protection and Reliance Act (filed 2025-04-02; referred to Rules 2025-04-03)
findings.note: Listed as a co-sponsor (not primary). Per the bill digest (https://webservices.ncleg.gov/BillDigests/2025/H691), the bill says courts and election boards must treat election rules and State Board directives in place on election day as binding, and bars excluding votes based on a law or procedure not in effect on election day. It does not itself set ID or citizenship rules. Saved as a related election-rules item. It stayed in committee.
subjects: rules applied to votes after election day
no-ID voter: affidavit, reasonable impediment, provisional ballot, free ID
